premise: At 59, after 27 years as a school custodian, I returned home to care for my dying father, who left me 60% of his 40-acre Christmas tree farm worth $480,000, but my sister forged a deed transferring my share to herself and sold the land to a holiday-lot chain for $690,000, handing me a $4,900 'wreath' check; I found the original will hidden inside a tin sap bucket, voided the sale, and now run 'Balsam of Betrayal Tree Farm,' where she prunes trees in a smock that says 'Sheared My Inheritance' and every tree tag prints her probate-fraud docket.
